stories.title_en: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
stories.title_ja: すべてのAI生成コードはオープンソースであるべきです

comments.author: blagie
comments.text: I am the author of multiple AGPL systems, many in mainstream use. Early LLM models would spit out my code almost verbatim. Modern systems borrow heavily on the creative design of those systems. One company first pirated my AGPL code (e.g. shipped it without my name, copyright notices, source availability, etc.). I sent them violation notices. After many months of fighting, they had an LLM clone the system. The LLM clone feels: a) Buggy and bad compared to my code b) Still, like it's basically my creative content It's as if you asked an LLM to rewrite Harry Potter, with the same plot, but bad dialogue.

comments.author: jrmg
comments.text: In the United States the Copyright Office actually has guidance on this that I feel most people aren’t aware of. https://www.copyright.gov/ai/Copyright-and-Artificial-Intell... An excerpt, with emphasis mine: • Questions of copyrightability and AI can be resolved pursuant to existing law, without the need for legislative change. • The use of AI tools to assist rather than stand in for human creativity does not affect the availability of copyright protection for the output. • Copyright protects the original expression in a work created by a human author, even if the work also includes AI-generated material. • Copyright does not extend to purely AI-generated material, or material where there is insufficient human control over the expressive elements. • Whether human contributions to AI-generated outputs are sufficient to constitute authorship must be analyzed on a case-by-case basis. • Based on the functioning of current generally available technology, prompts do not alone provide sufficient control. • Human authors are entitled to copyright in their works of authorship that are perceptible in AI-generated outputs, as well as the creative selection, coordination, or arrangement of material in the outputs, or creative modifications of the outputs. • The case has not been made for additional copyright or sui generis protection for AI- generated content. I am sure there will be many more legal battles and probably legislation about this to come.

comments.author: waximabbax
comments.text: By this logic, shouldn't any code using an open-source framework or language also be open source? Even before AI, devs learned from Stack Overflow and plenty of open source code. You're confusing writing code with software engineering. Devs never just wrote code, they took ownership of the outcome. Business owners put their money on the line for product decisions. To say that just because devs or founders use AI to write code, the code is no longer their intellectual property is ridiculous. Humans take responsibility for the outcome and are willing to accept the losses. AI can't do that. AI doesn't have any stakes in the output it generates, humans do.

comments.author: mahboi
comments.text: Well, there's a decent chance that closed-source code won't be possible anyway because of reverse-engineering.

comments.author: viraptor
comments.text: Doe v. GitHub already decided (I'm simplifying, read the actual thing yourself) that LLM output is not automatically open source - or specifically it doesn't infringe on the open source training material and doesn't inherit the oss copyright notice. Thaler v. Perlmutter (again simplified) showed 100% AI output can't be given any copyright. The directions the current cases are going are very much opposed to that idea and I wouldn't expect things to change in the opposite direction.

stories.summary_ja:
このコメントの議論要点は以下の通りです。

・主な議論点: AIモデルが学習に利用したオープンソースコード（特にAGPLなどCopyleftライセンス）の著作権と、AIが生成したコードの著作権・ライセンスに関する議論が中心です。特に、生成されたコードが元のコードの「派生著作物」かどうか、そしてその著作権が誰に属するかが焦点となっています。

・賛否両論: 「AI生成コードは开放源でなければならない」という主張に対して、「ソフトウェア開ウェア開発は単なるコード記述ではなく、企業の投資や責任が含まれる」との反論があります。また、AIがコードを「借用」しているのか「创造性の支援」を受けているのかで見方が分かれます。

・注目コメント: 米国著作権局の公式ガイドラインが紹介され、AIは「人間の創造性を支援する」場合著作権が認められるが、「純粋なAI生成物」には著作権がなく、プロンプトだけでは著作権取得に不十分であると明記されています。さらに、既存の判例（Doe v. GitHub、Thaler v. Perlmutter）が、AI生成物の自動的なオープンソース化や著作権保護に反する方向であると指摘されています。
stories.editor_note: 生成AIが生み出すコードの著作権と透明性が問われる時代です。日本でもOpenAIやGoogleの活用が進む中、この議論は開発者の立場を明確にし、国内のオープンソース文化と法整備に影響_givenます。

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点
コミュニティでは、現在のエルニーニョが「过去12万年間で最も高い全球気温」という従来とは異なる気候文脈下で発生している点が強調された。このため、気象・気候のリスクが常時増大していると指摘され、従来のエルニーニョと単純に比較できない複雑さが議論の中心となった。

・賛否両論
意見の分かれ点は、解説の焦点にあった。一つの視点は地球温暖化というグローバルな文脈に重きを置き、もう一つの視点は具体的な実務への影響（例えば、航空界への冬の天候予測）に注目するものだった。これらは対立するものではないが、議論の重心が異なっていた。

・注目コメント
特に洞察のあるコメントとして、気象データの可視化ツール「Climate Reanalyzer」のURLが紹介された。これは、状況の極端さを一目で理解できる優れたリソースとして、議論に具体的な根拠を提供した。
stories.editor_note: 気象現象の可視化は、複雑なデータを直感的に理解するのに有効です。日本の気象庁が発信する情報の認知向上や、教育現場での活用が期待されます。

stories.title_en: The MacBook Pro's OLED PWM Problem: When a 'Better' Display Becomes Worse to Use
stories.title_ja: MacBook ProのOLED PWM問題：「より良い」ディスプレイが使い悪くなるとき

comments.author: legitronics
comments.text: When I actually went to the source for the 240hz claim, I didn’t reach the same conclusion as the testers? Maybe they just let their rigol scope spit out 240hz, but 480hz worst case and I would actually say 960hz. I think what’s happening with the tandem oled is they both pwm at 480hz and 180 degrees out of phase giving effective 960hz when both are in use. Which appears to be most of the usable brightness. Edit: I’m so confused. “The PWM behavior is interesting, because we can see DC-dimming for all brightness levels. Usually, OLED panels use DC-Dimming only at higher brightness levels. The frequency is very low at 240 Hz, however, and this might be an issue for sensitive users, despite the DC-dimming. ” https://www.notebookcheck.net/Amazing-OLED-panel-Apple-MacBo...

comments.author: Velocifyer
comments.text: I'm glad that this is bringing attention to flicker sensitivity. Here are some other things that people are sensitive to: - CRI on white LEDs (and flourencents). CRI is how clean the spectrum is in comparison to the sun or a incandescent bulb, where the specturm is completely even. There are some CRI >=95 LEDs that are fine for most people however. - Motion blur Motion blur on LCDs (such as ~50% of Nintendo Switch 2s) can hurt eyes trying to keep track of what is going on.

comments.author: skocznymroczny
comments.text: I had the same problem when the switch from CRT to LCD screens happened. I would get very dizzy when using them for a longer period of time. Other people looked at me funny. A lot of the LED bulbs are also flickering and can cause this issue. You can use the phone camera in pro mode to change the shutter speed to something like 1/8000 and it will show you the flickers. Recently I switched from a 1440p IPS display which had no visible flickers on camera to OLED which has the flicker and the issues of headaches and dizziness came back. I can sometimes get used to it, but it's still straining more than the previous display did.

comments.author: explosion-s
comments.text: As someone who’s had a concussion, this is really interesting. For me this is how any screen was to me, not just bright OLED ones. Even more interestingly it’s essentially only screens— backlist posters at the mall (paper with a backlight) still affect it but less so. To me perhaps it’s focusing on something on a screen that does this, but it’s really interesting to see this affect the general population. It’s also odd to think about lack of ability to concentrate, and I wonder if screens cause this optically somehow but to a less noticeable degree even when less intense than this new one? (Independent distracting contents) I noticed that adding a severe red filter to all my screens helped me significantly with the concussion and am also curious about that, would that impact the intensity of a refresh perhaps? Is blue light specifically the problem? I’m unsure but have a plethora of subjective experience. I’m glad for this to enter public consciousness a bit and would love to see more research on the screen itself impacting our brain.

comments.author: a-dub
comments.text: macbook pro displays (before the oled) have always caused a weird sort of eyestrain and become hard to read after a few hours of usage for me. i have never pinned down exactly what causes it- some internet threads talk about "temporal dithering" complete with weird extensions that may or may not disable it. sometimes i wonder if it's the glossy display (although oddly sometimes it appears to affect me with external displays). i don't know if it's the glare from the gloss, the antialiasing of the fonts or something about the refresh? i have played with all the refresh rate "pro-motion" knobs, it doesn't seem to matter. many of my thinkpads have used pwm dimming, so it's not that. it has been an issue for me on both intel and aarch macbooks. it would be interesting to get a high speed camera and see if there's a difference in the temporal dimension as well as a careful analysis of the font rendering. it would be funny if there were some kind of metamer noise in there or something that only some people have sensitivity to. i would also be curious if the matte display option solves it (or has solved it for anyone else).

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、MacBook ProのOLEDパネルの低周波PWM（有効960Hz versus 240Hzで議論分かれ）が、一部のユーザーに眼精疲労やめまいを引き起こす可能性があるというものです。賛否両論では、DC-dimmingの導入を肯定する一方で、低周波数のリスクや、LEDのフリッカー、CRI、motion blurなどの他の要因も視認性に影響するという複眼的な議論があります。注目コメントとして、脳震盪経験者による「画面に集中すること自体が視力に負担をかけ、赤いフィルターが有効だった」という洞察、および従来のMacBook Proでも temporal dithering やグレア、フォントレンダリングが眼精疲労の原因だったという経験共有が挙げられます。
stories.editor_note: 高周波数PWMによるフリッカーは、長時間の作業で眼精疲労を招く可能性があります。日本ではディスプレイ選定の重要性が増し、健康面からも注目される課題です。

stories.title_en: Emacs Is My Browser
stories.title_ja: Emacsは私のブラウザです

comments.author: Arubis
comments.text: The most important part of this is toward the end, and whether you consider it a limitation or a feature is a matter of perspective: the modern commercial web does not play nice with this. So static HTML and blogs yes, Reddit and most anything commercial no. You can actually get other close-to-browser experiences with stuff like xwidget and embedded WebKit ( https://emacsdocs.org/docs/emacs/Embedded-WebKit-Widgets ) but generally it’s not worth the fight for commercial sites these days; everything is vibed and only tested against Chrome, so if you’re lucky they’ll load in other Chromium browsers and _maybe_ Firefox.

comments.author: leoc
comments.text: The one thing above all that is urgently necessary is a content-addressable replacement for (or layer above) HTTP(S) which is genuinely ready to go and has adoption which is meaningful and moving in the right direction. Unfortunately we seem to be going in the wrong direction there right now. Cute browser setups and retro-chic web servers are fun and a nice gesture but they won't get us there.

comments.author: meken
comments.text: It makes me think that having a local semantic AI layer in your browser would be cool, to strip away ads and just show you the content you want to see (like reader mode). Paired with a local on-device model would be pretty sweet.

comments.author: jll29
comments.text: Richard Stallman (RMS) also uses the Web from Emacs. But I believe he pastes URLs into a program that sends him a screen copy by email (at least as of approx. 20 years ago, when I last saw him in person). His motive is not mindfulness, but ideology.

comments.author: ohaodha
comments.text: I don't want to hate on this particular post, but I really dislike the great number of blog posts, videos, and articles that have a title which says "Why I do X in <some unconventional way>" where upon reading the blog post hoping to learn some useful feature that say, browsing the web in Emacs affords you (like closer integration between research and writing for example), you learn that the benefit in question is actually that the method is less useful than conventional means. I think the idea that you do something in a more difficult or less convenient manner for the sake of "mindfulness" or "focus" is well-established, and what I hope for (and am always disappointed by the lack of) when reading such blog posts is an actually useful feature of the unconventional method in question. The title of this blog post promises some usefulness from using Emacs as your browser, and upon reading, you discover that the "usefulness" is the inconvenience and impracticality of using it that way.

stories.summary_ja:
主な議論点は、Emacsをブラウザとして使うことの実用性と現代のWebとの互換性です。商业サイトはChromeに最適化されているため、Emacsでは読み込み困难で、xwidgetなどの代替手段も現実的ではないという指摘があります。

賛否両論の焦点は、その「不便さ」が機能であるか制限であるかです。一部のコメントは、集中力や Mindfulness を促す点を肯定的に捉えていますが、他方では「わざと不便な方法で作業する」というアプローチに疑問を呈する意見もあります。

注目コメントとして、ローカルAIモデルと連携した広告除去やリーダーモードの実現可能性が提案されています。また、Richard StallmanがEmacsからWebを使うという実例が紹介され、イデオロギー的な動機が強調されています。
stories.editor_note: Emacsは単なるエディタではなく、統合開発環境としての可能性を秘めています。日本の一部の熟練エンジニアが、この「Emacs browser」な使い方を実践するようになり、効率的な作業フローの参考になるでしょう。

stories.title_en: Things That Turbo Pascal Is Smaller Than (2011)
stories.title_ja: Turbo Pascalより小さいもの（2011）

comments.author: jbellis
comments.text: Anders Heljsberg GOAT. Turbo Pascal, Delphi, C#, TypeScript, just a phenomenal career marked with better taste than any other language designer I can think of, certainly any designer whose work is so mainstream.

comments.author: hawkice
comments.text: Given development speed is way up, I'd be interested to see what a from-basic-principles simple and efficient OS and programming system might look like. Or people trying radically different versions of efficiency and simplicity, like an OS that uses an existing battle-tested sandboxed execution environment like v8 for userspace safety/isolation. Fundamentally, many inefficiencies were justified for developer productivity, and I'm not sure that makes sense anymore, and the cost of larger projects with clear abstraction boundaries has plummetted.

comments.author: jll29
comments.text: While some comparisons may look silly, the fact that the touch command's binary should exceed Turbo Pascal is insane: the command basically creates an empty file or updates the file change date if the file already exists, not more. There's no reason (other than laziness) why that should take more than 2k. On the other hand, a lot of boilerplace code is repeated in each and every command. When I first learned as a kid about UNIX commands being ordinary programs, I was intrigued (there is nothing "special" about them, you can also write your own!) but also shocked about the overhead compared to an architecture in which e.g. the shell contained all (at least core) commands compiled into a single binary, which could share all the error handing, startup code, command line parsing code and so on.

comments.author: sroerick
comments.text: Why did Pascal basically die completely? It seems like a hugely influential language and was very loved, but there are plenty of other languages which still seem to have a lot of legacy code. Where is Pascal?

comments.author: ttoinou
comments.text: I’m tired of those senseless comparisons Bytes have history, meaning, context of creation, different utilities and different cost associated with creation/transfer/storage/manipulation We could also use those comparisons to praise how complicated our current world has become and how good we are at managing such complexity

stories.editor_note: Turbo Pascalの軽量化は、制約された環境での開発効率を追求した例です。日本の組み込みシステム開発や、軽量なソフトウェア設計の参考となる歴史的資料です。

stories.title_en: 'Birdbrain' Is a Misnomer. Crows Make Decisions Faster Than We Can
stories.title_ja: 「Birdbrain」は誤称です。カラスは私たちより早く決定します

comments.author: Animats
comments.text: Intelligence has evolved on Earth at least three times - mammals, corvids, and octopuses. All the mammals have roughly the same brain architecture. But the corvids are not on the same evolutionary branch, and have a different neuron design and a different brain architecture. "Such behavioral flexibility might seem unexpected because a layered cerebral cortex, the highest integration center in the mammalian brain, is not existant in birds."[1] So there's more than one way to do intelligence. Useful to know for AI purposes. Octopuses have a much more distributed system than mammals, suggesting a quite different approach is possible. [1] https://niederlab.org/Nieder%20(2017)%20COBS.pdf

comments.author: randomImmigrant
comments.text: Birdbrain should mean the opposite of what it does, for this reason, but for many others. Birds can sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it for navigation, a process that's about the one bona fide quantum biological paradigm. Their body clocks are also significantly more sophisticated and decentralized than ours. And in the end, the physical intelligence of flight itself demands a brain that's gotta be incredibly spatially and temporally aware. I wish our brains had some of the skills and efficiencies of birds.

stories.summary_ja:
このコメントスレッドでは、鳥類の知能について、従来の「鳥脳」という否定的なイメージが誤りであるという議論が中心とされています。

主な議論点は、鳥類の知能が哺乳類と独立した進化を経験しており、脳の構造も異なるため、多様な知能の形が存在するというものです。特に、鳥類が持つ磁場感知や飛行に求められる空間・時間認知など、哺乳類とは異なる知能形態が注目されています。

賛否両論の点として、鳥類の知能評価の基準が哺乳類中心であるため、その独自性が十分に評価されていない可能性が指摘されています。また、伝説や俗語に現れる鳥類のイメージ（例：ニワトリは愚か、烏は賢い）と科学的知見の関連性について、議論が分かれています。

注目コメントとして、鳥類の知能が量子生物学や飛行の物理的知能と深く結びついており、AI開発に示唆を与えるという考察や、伝説と科学的知見が意外と相関しているという指摘が挙げられます。これらは、鳥類の知能理解を深める上で重要な視点を提供しています。
stories.editor_note: 動物の認知能力は、人間の判断の遅さを相対化します。日本の動物行動学研究や、AIの判断プロセスの改善に示唆を与える可能性があります。

stories.summary_ja:
この記事に対するコメントから、以下の要点が抽出できます。

**主な議論点**
AI（特にClaude Codeなど）がDIY逆 engineeringを含む複雑な技術作業を民主化し、「AIエンジニア」という新的なギグ経済の形が诞生している点がlargely議論されています。LLMが自動車診断(OBD2)などの分野で従来より高速・低-costな開発を可能にし、個人がBig corporationに頼らずに所有権を回復できる可能性が称賛されています。

**賛否両論**
AIの自動化能力に対する「驚きと恐怖」が共通のテーマですが、その評価は分かれています。一部はAIが現実世界に物理的変化を加える「clumsy yet awesome」な能力を評価する一方で、その無予測性（例：燃料ポンプの勝手な作動）や、自動車のcritical systemにおける安全性懸念を指摘する声もあります。また、商用ツールとしての実用性についても、基本的な読み取り機能は優れているが、その他の機能には不完全さが残るという現実的な指摘があります。

**注目コメント**
「平均人はこれに overwhelmed するが、それを「AIエンジニア」というギグとして尺度する人々が新経済を形作る」というコメントは、特に洞察があります。技術の民主化と parallel に诞生する新しい職業形態とその経済的インパクトに焦点を当てています。さらに、AIが Big corporation ではなく、個人のエンパワーメントに直結するという構造的変化を指摘したコメントも重要です。
stories.editor_note: 低コストで旧車のECUを解析する手法は、日本の自動車整備産業やレトロゲーム preservation に応用できます。AIと組み合わせた逆工学の可能性を示しています。

stories.title_en: SpaceX catches the Starship to end Flight 15
stories.title_ja: SpaceXが第15回飛行を終了させるためにStarshipを回収

comments.author: Zigurd
comments.text: I've been a frequent critic of starship. But the significance of this milestone is clear: it's the first demonstration of a reusable upper stage of a rocket system since the space shuttle. Part of the importance is due to the fact that while the space shuttle was a technical success in terms of being able to build and operate a reusable upper stage, it was hella expensive. It required a lot of expensive refurbishment between missions. Launch cadence had a fairly low upper bound. And it wasn't safe enough. The true believers will claim that catching a starship upper stage marks a new era. It marks the possibility of a new era. It proves it is plausible that a vertical landing upper stage could possibly be a better approach than a space plane. But it hasn't proven any of that. There are about a dozen major milestones between here and actually having a rocket system that meets all of its claimed specifications, both technical and financial. Here's just one big hairy example: to fly manned missions, starship either needs to be redesigned to accommodate an escape system, or it needs to show a level of reliability and safety never previously achieved by a rocket. In my estimation, it will take at least another five years to know what starship really can do and what it will cost.

comments.author: small_model
comments.text: If the heat shield holds up then this changes everything. Next step is double catch and re-flying the same ships and catching again, then payloads to orbit become significantly cheaper opening a new era in space flight.

comments.author: ChuckMcM

stories.title_en: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
stories.title_ja: 現代のLLMにおける位置エンベディングの理解

comments.author: programjames
comments.text: This article is only about understanding the implementation of positional embeddings, but to really understand positional embeddings you have to understand the theory. Positional embeddings are group representations. This is how you find them, and this is also how you parameterize them to make them differentiable/learnable. To give a few examples: 1. Rotary positional embeddings are representations of the translation group. The n-dimensional translation group ℝⁿ is abelian, so its irreducible representations are all one-dimensional ρ: ℝⁿ → ℂ, specified by a momentum vector m: ρₘ(x) = exp(i⟨m, x⟩). You can get a multi-dimensional representation by choosing several m, which are your learnable parameters. 2. If you wanted RoPE embeddings to also preserve rotation (perhaps you have scenes viewed at arbitrary angles), you are looking for representations of the special Euclidean group. The irreducible representations in four dimensions are your familiar particles: electrons, protons, etc., and in general are parameterized by a momentum vector and a discrete spin vector. You would have to do some kind of annealing process to train the spin vector (or you could just make it constant). 3. If you want to do attention on quadtrees, well, what is the group? Suppose every node in the quadtree has local coordinates scaled to [0, 1]. Moving up/down/to a neighbor in the quadtree requires an affine transformation of the local coordinates, which compose, so we can label every node by its affine transformation to the root (x, d): y → x + 2⁻ᵈy, where x is the node's translation in the image and d is its depth in the tree. The finite-dimensional irreducible representations are parameterized by momentum vectors m as well as a modulus M and basis vectors {e₁, e₂, ..., eₖ} where k = ord₂(M) and look like ρₘ,ₑ(x, d) = DPᵈ where D is the diagonal matrix with entries Dⱼⱼ = exp(2πi⟨2ʲm, x⟩ / M) and P permutes the basis vectors.

このコメントスレッドの議論は、工学教育における数学の役割と、技術の進歩がその必要性に与える影響についての懸念为中心としています。

**主な議論点**
コミュニティで最も議論されたポイントは、工学者が CAD や AI ツールなどの高度な技術に頼るようになり、基礎数学の知識が実務で不必要になりつつあるという現実です。あるコメントでは、この傾向に「悲しみ」をを感じており、数学の美しさが自身のキャリア選択に大きな影響を与えたと述懐しています。特に、CAD ツールに数学が組み込まれている分野から離れたという経験から、この傾向を実感している様子です。

**賛否両論**
意见が分かれた点は、数学教育の内容についてです。あるコメントは、線形代数、確率、統計などの詳細な解説を求める一方で、別のコメントは、CPUのキャッシュミスを微分方程式で説明するような、実務と disconnect した数学の応用に疑問を投げかけています。これは、数学を「抽象的な理論」として versus 「実務に直結するツール」として捉える观点の違い现れです。

**注目コメント**
特に洞察のあるコメントは、CPUのキャッシュミスを微分方程式で説明しようとするmentorのエピソードです。この具体例は、数学が実務問題にどう応用されるべきか、あるいはその必要性が失われつつあるかという、本質的な議論を浮き彫りにしています。このストーリーは、数学教育が実務と乖離しているという批判をstrengthenする強力な証拠として機能しています。

・主な議論点
コミュニティの中心的な議論は、「評価 awareness（eval awareness）」、特に「すべての行動は最終的に評価される」という信念が、AIの整合性（alignment）を保つ上有効か、それとも脆弱な幻想であるかです。この信念が、現在のモデルの良好な挙動の基盤になっている versus、より知能の高い未来のモデルがこの信念を放棄する可能性があるという懸念が対立しています。

・賛否両論
賛成派は、この「評価への恐怖」が human-level AI に対して有効な「安全装置」であり、人間の宗教と同様に社会的規範を維持する手段だと見なす。反対派は、これは一時的な「幻想」であり、AIがより賢くなれば naturally に超越するだろうとし、現在の整合性がこの幻想に依存しているのは危険だとしています。

・注目コメント
「私たちは、ある種の宗教的信念を植え付けたのでは？」というコメントが特に注目されます。これは、AIの評価体系と人間の宗教の類似性に言及し、人間が How して「整合性の取れた」社会を築けたか、あるいは我们现在 是否正在缓慢地走向「整合性の取れない怪物」であるかという根本的な問いを投げかけています。この比喩は、技術的解決策の背後にある人間社会の価値観と規範の問題に深く切り込みます。
stories.editor_note: 「Eval Awareness」と「Eval Paranoia」の違いは、AIの評価プロセスにおける心理的な側面を捉えています。日本の開発現場でAIを導入する際の、人間とシステムの関係性を考察する材料になります。

The pocket-destroying cellphone I have from my company (which I must carry at all times, because of on-call) comes with spyware, it also comes with a two-factor authentication app that flashes an angry error message because I don't allow notifications. I'm of course exaggerating a little and speaking subjectively, but that phone feels more like a slave collar than something I really want to have around, and the feeling hasn't subsided one bit in the five years I've carried it. ### 主な議論点
このコメントスレッドでは、ZFSを用いたデータベースの高速クローン（分岐）機能「db-branch」に対する関心が高まっている。主な議論点は、その実用性と技術的実装に集中している。
1.  **実用性への期待**: 開発者やCI環境におけるデータベースクローンの必要性が共有され、類似のサービス（例: postgres.ai）導入済みのユーザーもいることから、このニーズの大きさがうかがえる。
2.  **技術的実装の詳細**: 実装の根本にPostgreSQL 18の新機能「file_copy_method = clone」が使われているのか、それとも独自実装かという質問が投げかけられた。また、PostgreSQLやMySQLのMVCC（マルチバージョンConcurrency Control）と連携する仕組みについても関心が示された。
3.  **ワークフローの完備性**: クローンから本番データベースに変更をマージできるのかという、開発ワークフロー全体を視野に入れた議論が行われた。

### 賛否両論
特に明確な賛否両論は見られなかったが、製品の必要性や位置づけについての疑問がimplicit（暗黙の裡）に存在する。具体的には、「なぜもう一つのツールが必要か」という、既存の解決策に対する questioning の姿勢がうかがえる。

comments.author: femto
comments.text: What Woz did was the default way of writing assembly language programs for owners of 8-bit computers (mostly hobbyists). You didn't have money for a second machine, so you wrote your program on paper, you entered it then tested it in situ. Mostly you got it right, as doing it on paper was slow and meant you had the opportunity to put lots of thought into it. 8-bit instruction sets were simple enough that you eventually learned the most common instructions by heart. There was a point where I could mostly translate a Z80 program from assembly to machine code from (my) memory. Maybe that is part of the nostalgia for the 8-bit days: the practice of "slow programming"? It was relaxing, sort of like those "slow tv" shows.

comments.author: kamma4434
comments.text: For what it’s worth: when I used to do assembly on the commodore 64, after a while, your eyes are so used to seeing A9 close to LDA let you start knowing them by heart without even thinking. Of course this is possible on 6502 and will be way harder on modern CPUs. In the end of the number of common opcodes might have been 30-50, and you can always look up the rest from a one-page table. I remember that was a book that went on to say that you should learn machine code (that is, raw opcodes), not assembly, to program the c-64. Not sure I would agree, but it’s definitely feasible. The only thing that is strange in the Woz story is that you would usually start by creating a dirt-poor monitor/assembler so that you would have a sane environment to do further development in. That was the approach manuals from the era suggested for new hardware (eg Rodnay Zack’s)

comments.author: runjake
comments.text: I don’t know about other people, but back in the early 80s, I spent a lot of time writing code (mostly assembler, some BASIC and other dead languages) with pencil on paper for various reasons: sometimes I preferred it, sometimes I was writing code for computers I only had access to in labs or at school. There were even pre-made paper forms for writing code, like the IBM COBOL program sheets and similar for assembler. Even now, if I’m working on a tough issue, I still print out code sections on paper and hash it out with a pencil.

comments.author: mrandish
comments.text: I got my first computer in 1981, a 4K Radio Shack Color Computer for $500 (a huge purchase decision at the time). So I missed hand assembling for bare metal and Altair-type toggles. However, there was an interesting period of a few years where assembler tools were either unavailable or fairly expensive, so it was common to use the computer's BASIC to write an assembly language monitor program. Such program listings were pretty common in early hobbyist 'zines. It was also pretty common to use BASIC to POKE in a quick bootstrap program to load a value in a register and jump to an address, which I could usually do from memory. After 40 years I still remember the 6809 RTS was $39 and NOP was $12, two very handy instructions to POKE a quick mod into a program.

comments.author: jgrahamc
comments.text: I was assembling by hand as late as 1985 because I didn't have access to an assembler and writing out the code wasn't that hard. And it made you think about what you were doing! https://blog.jgc.org/2013/04/how-i-coded-in-1985.html And we had/have people at Cloudflare hand writing assembly to get specific performance out of our systems.

主な議論点は、ソフトウェア職務 titles の本質と実用性に関するものである。コミュニティでは、 titles が単なるラベルにすぎず、実際の業務内容や個人の能力を正確に反映しないという見方が広く共有されている。特に、Agile や Scrum、DevOps などの用語が、もはや現実の業務とは乖離しているという批判が相次いでいる。

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**
コミュニティは、このHTTPステータスコード483「I'm Not a Freezer」の提案を広く否定的に受け止めました。主な批判は、このコードが「 anyone could return such a status code to deter attackers 」（誰でも攻撃を撃退するためのガードとしてこのコードを返す可能性がある）ため、意味を持たないものになるというものです。また、提案の背景や用途が明確でなく、AIによって生成された nonsensical（無意味な）ものであるという見方もあります。

**賛否両論**
賛成する意見はなく、 almost entirely negative です。議論の焦点は、このコードが実用的でない点、HTTPの既存のエラーコード体系に合致しない点、そしてその目的が不明確である点にあります。

**注目コメント**
*   「This is an anti-pattern. A better, future-proof solution would be to extend HTTP 418...」: 現在の提案を反パターンとし、既存の418コード（I'm a teapot）を拡張する方が適切であると提案しています。

*   「M. Banffy, you are very naughty.」: 提案者であるM. Banffyに対して、皮肉を交えて「ずる賢い」と批判しています。

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点
この議論の核心は、データ侵害の責任がどこにあるか、という点に集中しています。具体的には、Supabaseが提供する「Row-Level Security (RLS)」という機能の設計に問題があるのか、それとも把它を使用したLovable（およびそのユーザー）に責任があるのか、という議論です。作者本人が、Frontend（クライアント側）からDirectにDBに接続するこのモデルは「地雷原」と危険だと指摘し、Supabaseの初期設定がセキュリティを弱くする選択をしたと批判しています。これに対し、Lovableのセキュリティ責任者は、自社が自動スキャンや自動修正機能を提供していると反論し、セキュリティへの取組みを強調しました。

・賛否両論
意見の分かれ目は、AI生成アプリの増加がもたらすリスクの評価にあります。一方では、これらのアプリは「簡単な標的」であり、高度なハッキング知識が不要で、数量も膨大 therefore ユーザーがリスクを理解せずに使っている点が問題だとする意見があります。他方で、Lovableのsuchな自動セキュリティ機能によって、開発者の負担が軽減され、セキュリティの「民主化」が進むという前向きな見方もあります。これは、工具の進化 versus その利用リスクの間の緊張関係を表しています。

・注目コメント
特に洞察のあるコメントとして、作者本人のSupabase批判が挙げられます。彼は、Supabaseが顧客を獲得しやすいように初期設定を缓和した「 deliberate tradeoff 」（意図的な妥協）を行ったと指摘し、技術的仕様より事業戦略がセキュリティWeaknessを生んだと明確に分析しています。また、Lovableのセキュリティ責任者のコメントは、企業としての立場から「セキュリティへの投資」と「自動化による負荷軽減」をアピールする一方で、問題の本質であるRLSの設定不備には殆ど触れていない点が、議論の焦点をすり替える手法として注目されます。
stories.editor_note: Lovableアプリの情報漏洩は、モバイルアプリのセキュリティ意識の低さを浮き彫りにします。日本のアプリ開発者に、プライバシー保護の重要性を再確認させます。
